headline: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.voteItem: Rename a Water Supply project to countywide facility improvements
meeting.summary: The committee removed police radio project funding, raised the small-grant limit to $30,000, and lowered the emergency fund by $32 million.
meeting.recap: Staff said the committee stood at about $30 million in cuts and just over $40 million in additions.[[0:04:24]] An engineer testified that a regional wastewater project for a bay community may cost $12.48 million to $16.14 million.[[0:23:19]] The committee removed bond funding for a police radio upgrade that the department said it could not use next year.[[4:45:27]] A member proposed a $500,000 zero-interest loan to design a private wastewater plant for part of a country town development.[[6:06:08]] The member withdrew the loan motion for now.[[6:17:02]] The committee lowered the emergency fund total by $32 million already authorized for the storms.[[7:10:18]] A member proposed a $1-per-minute idle fee at County EV chargers, starting five minutes after charging ends.[[7:12:01]] The committee planned to return the next day at 9 a.m. to take public testimony.[[7:30:28]]
decided: The committee corrected a Department of Water Supply project name in Bill 55 to match Bill 60.
The committee changed the funding type for Molokaʻi reliable capacity from unrestricted to restricted water funds.
The committee fixed the wording of water usage tiers so the ranges do not overlap; the rates stay the same.
The committee cut $150,000 for a PGA tournament after the organization pulled out.
The committee set the small-grant limit at up to $30,000 per grant.
The committee reduced the small grants pot, leaving it at $1.6 million.
The committee removed bond funding for police radio system upgrades at the department's request.
The committee cut $550,000 from a countywide Public Works base yard facilities project.
The committee rewrote the Lānaʻi food voucher grant condition to give preference to seniors age 60 and up and children.
The committee reduced the community development block grant program by $269,935.
The committee reduced the emergency fund by $32 million already authorized for the storms.
meeting.next: Staff will give members an Excel template to work on real property tax proposals. Members discussed drafting a resolution urging the administration to fund the wastewater loan from carryover savings.

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: Testifiers urged funding for a regional wastewater system to improve water quality in a Maui bay.
issues.why: An engineer said the bay is on the EPA's list of impaired water bodies and has less than 5% living coral.
issues.next: The engineer described one year for design and permitting and one year for construction, pending funding.
issues.brief: The engineer said the project may cost $12.48 million to $16.14 million.[[#1]] The committee fixed a typo so a Molokaʻi water project is paid from restricted water funds.[[#2]] A fix to water usage tier wording left the water rates the same.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: A member proposed a $500,000 zero-interest loan to design a private wastewater plant for part of a country town development.
issues.why: The member said the project is stalled while waiting on the County plant, and the community needs its affordable housing and school.
issues.next: Members discussed a resolution urging the administration to fund the loan from carryover savings.
issues.brief: A member said the Central Maui wastewater facility may not be working until 2031.[[#1]] The loan motion was withdrawn for now.[[#2]] The committee cut the community development block grant line by $269,935 to match the award letter.[[#3]]
